title: Above-fold content viewed more than below-fold
statement:
NN/g's eyetracking analysis of 57,453 fixations found the 100 pixels just above the fold were viewed 102% more than the 100 pixels just below it (about an 84% average difference when combined with Google's ad-viewability data), so the most important content and calls to action should sit above the fold, with cues that encourage scrolling.

Options:
- Design for each device's fold: Value proposition and primary CTA fully visible at each target breakpoint, designing for each device's own fold (fits: professional, clear, conversion-focused)
- Signposts and anchors: Signposts near the top of long pages, such as anchor links or previews of what comes next (fits: organized, helpful, editorial)
- Reward for scrolling: Interesting content or engaging imagery at and just below the fold that rewards scrolling and builds the story (fits: storytelling, warm, bold)
- Avoid false floors: Visible cut-off content instead of a lone arrow, to avoid a false floor (fits: modern, clear, confident)
appliesWhen: Applies to: general web. Audience: general.

source.title: The Fold Manifesto: Why the Page Fold Still Matters
